newsitem.title: TOGO: World Bank promises Togo $114 mln, premier says.
newsitem.headline: World Bank promises Togo $114 mln, premier says.

text.p: The World Bank has promised Togo 57 billion CFA francs ($114 million) in aid for a range of projects, Prime Minister Kwassi Kultse told the nation on his return from talks in Washington.
The money could be spent on such things health, roads and energy projects, he added in remarks on state radio and television on Friday night.
Klutse said that if Togo achieved its macro-economic targets "the aid expected from the Bank could rise from 57 to 90 billion CFA for 1997 and 1998".
He added that a mission from the International Monetary Fund, with whom he also had talks in Washington, would visit Togo in the coming days to discuss their economic reform programme.
Togo was one of Africa top performing economies in 1995 as far as Gross Domestic Product growth was concerned. It topped eight percent against a continental average of between two and three percent.
